desc:
A garden has n plots in a row, numbered 0 to n - 1. Each sprinkler is described by [left, right] and waters every plot from left to right inclusive. A plot may be reached by several sprinklers.

Return how many plots are watered by at least k different sprinklers.

n = 6, sprinklers = [[0, 2], [1, 4], [3, 5], [2, 3]], k = 2
result = 4

The coverage counts per plot are [1, 2, 3, 3, 2, 1], and four plots have a count of 2 or more.
hints: If you could get the coverage count of every plot, the answer would be a simple count of plots with count ≥ k.
Adding 1 to every plot of every sprinkler is too slow in total. Mark only where each sprinkler starts and where it stops.
Use diff[left] += 1 and diff[right + 1] -= 1, sweep with a running sum, and count the plots where the running sum is at least k.
editorial: The coverage of plot i is the number of sprinklers whose range contains i. A difference array computes all coverages at once: +1 where a range starts and -1 just after it ends. The prefix sum of this array is the coverage.
A final pass counts the plots with coverage at least k. Total time O(n + m), space O(n). This +1/-1 sweep is the building block of many 'how many things overlap here' problems.
